This is Tier H (`docs/adr/**`). The maintainer's standing word for this project (2026-10-27, on #26566 / #26570): a Tier H PR goes to approvers only after the director seat's contract review PASS and the seat's ACCEPT; #26617 records why the relay's reviewer request at `pr_create` is not that signal. Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75285daf4f1e4acd3475391b33c4a318d4671616`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md + scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the gate the D9 note binds; read whole at the head and on `main`), and the cited code those hunks make claims about, read unchanged: scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs (`maskComments`), .changeset/config.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, ui/packages/plugin-ai/package.json (the first consumer's base manifest), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (the job that runs `--self-test` and `--base`). The diff has two files and both are in scope; no remainder goes to the lane seat at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #26220 body and all 14 comments (the claim 6444671327, the dispatch order 6444498687, the ruling pointer 6439050525, the four os-dev reports); PR #26766 body, file list, its one comment 6445680015 and its one review; the net diff against `main` at the head (one commit, +302/-10, 2 files, matching files.txt); 46 check-runs on the head; the ruling 6439038287 on PR #26365, plus that PR's body and its two earlier `Check Changeset` comments (6431333164, 6435952905), fetched read-only.

Gate verdicts on the head (the check-runs ARE the verdicts): 46 runs, all `completed`; 29 `success`, 17 `skipped` (UI lanes and opt-ins filtered), 0 failures, 0 in progress. `Check Changeset` (success, 15:00:50Z) is the pr-automation job whose step "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" runs `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --self-test` then `--base "$MERGE_BASE"`, so the gate's self-test exit 0 on this head is CI-measured, not only claimed. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (both runs) and `PR-body guards` are green.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong:

1. **The gate's accept-set widens by exactly one shape and nothing else — right, with one wrong limb (item 3).** `parseExportOperand` admits `PACKAGE#*` only when the spelling is literally `*` (`#**`, `#*x` and a bare `#*` stay refused: WP-U2); every other operand parses as before with `whole: false`. The whole-package branch runs only on `op.whole`; the export and member paths are untouched except for the appended `#*` hint on the "cannot be read at HEAD" refusal, which fires only when `packagesAt(head)` lacks the package (WP-R13). The 627 pre-existing assertions and their pins are unchanged in the diff. No existing green becomes red, no existing red becomes green.

2. **Predicate 1's package proof matches the amended text, and the text stays inside the ruling — right.** Ruling: "in the workspace with a published entry at the merge base; absent from the workspace at HEAD (no `package.json`, not in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, not in the changesets fixed group)". `verifyWholePackageRetired` reads, at the base: `packagesAt(base)` membership (enumerated from that rev's own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` via `workspaceGlobsAt`, #26319), `private` refused, `sourceEntryAt` mappable (the D9 mapping, `src/index.ts` or `src/index.tsx`, both-present refused as ambiguous). At HEAD: the base manifest path gone (`showOrNull(head, atBase.file) === null`), no workspace manifest of that name at another path, no literal glob equal to the package directory in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `.changeset/config.json` present, parseable, with no `fixed` group containing the name; a missing or non-array `fixed` is refused, never read as empty. Every failing HEAD condition is listed, not only the first (WP-R4 asserts two). Each elaboration beyond the ruling's nine words refuses more and admits nothing more: "not private" and "maps as above" are what D9 already means by "published entry" ("A private package has no published entry"; "an entry that cannot be mapped is refused"); "no glob names its directory literally" is the only reading of "not in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`" under which the ruling's own first consumer can exist (plugin-ai sits under `ui/packages/*`, which stays); the config-missing refusal is the gate's standing #4690 posture. Measured on `main`: `.changeset/config.json` lists every fixed member by literal name (108 entries, `@object-ui/plugin-ai` among them), `linked` is `[]`, no glob entries — so the literal reading loses nothing today, and it matches the condition's purpose (a stale literal name breaks `changeset version`; a glob cannot). Right.

3. **Predicate 2's package reading narrows D9's existing predicate 2 — wrong (must-fix 1).** The note writes "no metadata surface outside it imports it in code, by its root or a subpath", and `packageImporter` reads exactly that: a `from`, bare `import`, `import(` or `require(` specifier naming the package or a subpath, comment spans masked, own files skipped (WP-U3/U4, G3, R10 pin it). But D9's predicate 2 for an operand is "no metadata surface references it in code: the D7 primitives", and the D7 primitive the gate shares for exports, `metadataSurfaceReference`, refuses on an import **or on a bare code mention** — with string literals deliberately left unmasked (gate header: "STRING LITERALS ARE NOT MASKED, on purpose … the conservative direction here is to REFUSE (#4690) and a string is where an authorable value lives — a name in one may be doing work … a future widening to `comment || literal` has to be argued rather than slipped in"). A package name can appear in code only inside a string, so for this operand "references in code" collapses to "names it in any non-comment string"; the amendment keeps only the import-specifier subset and admits a metadata surface that carries the package name as a value (a plugin id, a package reference in an object definition). The ruling fixed predicates 1 and 3 and said nothing about 2, so it grants no authority to narrow 2; the PR body's own claim that predicate 2 "asks the package what it asks an export" is not what the code does. Measured on `main`: the four `@object-ui/plugin-ai` mentions in metadata surfaces (`ui/packages/types/src/zod/ai.zod.ts` ×3, `zod/index.zod.ts`) are all comment spans, so the first consumer is unaffected either way, and the fix is one predicate plus one sentence plus one red case.

4. **Predicate 3 reads the package's FROM line as the operand's spelling — right, one wording point (③-c).** A FROM operand whose `canonicalFromOperand` is null and whose tick-stripped text equals a `#*` package's name is re-read as that spelling; "exactly the named operands" then runs unchanged, so a per-export FROM line is out of range (WP-R12) and a missing package line is "no FROM side" (WP-R11). The FROM-line and arrow forms both reach it (G1, G2). Right.

5. **Refusal text — right.** An export or member operand on a package deleted at HEAD keeps its predicate-1 refusal and gains the `PACKAGE#*` remedy, as the note says.

6. **Public surface: none — right.** The root package is `private`; `scripts/**` and `docs/adr/**` are not published; `packages/spec` is untouched (no schema, no accept-set of any published artifact moves). `parseExportOperand`'s return shape gains `whole` and a nullable `exportName`, and `packageImporter` is newly exported; `git grep` over the head finds no importer of either outside the script. Internal only.

7. **Self-test roster — right.** `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` 57 → 58, battery `WP (#26220)` pinned at 50; the pins are floors (a battery reds only when its count falls below the pin), and the diff's own arithmetic is 3 greens + G1b + 13 reds (13 + 29 regexes) + U1–U4 = 50 exactly, 627 + 50 = 677 as the body states. CI measured exit 0; the counts are consistent with the diff.

8. **ADR text, Status line — right.** One new `Amended (2026-10-27, #26220, ruling A on PR #26365, comment 6439038287 …)` entry, pointing at "the second 2026-10-27 amendment note under D9's unmappable-entry paragraph", which is where the note sits. The note's provenance line names the comment, the letter and the maintainer's 「同意」 time.

9. **ADR text, the closed vocabulary — wrong (must-fix 2).** The 2026-08-13 addendum's code block ("The vocabulary is closed") and the 2026-10-12 addendum's block ("two operand kinds that may be mixed in one marker") still list only `PACKAGE#Export` and `PACKAGE#Type.member`, while `parseExportOperand` at the head accepts a third spelling. The grammar the ADR declares closed is now narrower than the grammar the gate enforces; the new note is the only place the spelling appears.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is correct: nothing in the diff publishes (root `private`, `scripts/**` and `docs/adr/**` unshipped, `packages/spec` untouched), so no package's version moves and no changeset is owed. `Clause-②: no` is correct — no published accept-set narrows or widens; `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct — no protocol major, no conversion, no deprecation entry. The os-dev `deviations` entry explaining why the dispatch order's "Changeset in the root `.changeset/`" was not followed is right on the facts.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

- **(a) Predicate 2's package reading (PR body "Acceptance notes", report deviation 4).** Judged against the ruling: outside it — the ruling is silent on predicate 2, so the note may only restate D9's predicate 2 for the new operand, not re-cut it. Judged against D9's existing text: narrower — "references it in code: the D7 primitives" became "imports it", dropping the code-mention limb the shared primitive applies to every other operand. **Not accepted; must-fix 1** (text + gate + one red case: a metadata surface outside the package that names it in a non-comment string). Expected text: "no metadata surface outside it names it in code — an import specifier, by its root or a subpath, or any other non-comment occurrence of the package name (comment spans masked, as `metadataSurfaceReference` reads)". Expected gate: `packageImporter` (or a sibling) refuses on the first comment-masked occurrence of the package name outside the package's own files, reporting the line; WP-G3 stays green, WP-R10 stays red, a new WP red pins the string-value mention.
- **(b) "Its exports take no line of their own" (same two flags).** Judged inside the ruling and inside D9: the ruling says the block "names the package on one line", and D9's predicate 3 already refuses any FROM operand the marker does not name; with the package as the operand, an export's FROM line is out of range by existing text. The sentence states a consequence, not a new rule. **Accepted.**
- **(c) "on **one** line" (text) vs the gate.** The gate does not count: two FROM lines both naming the package pass, exactly as predicate 3 has always tolerated a repeated FROM line for an export. The text's emphasised "one" reads as "one line rather than one per export", which the gate enforces; if a count is meant, the gate does not enforce it. Should-fix with must-fix 1 or 2: drop the emphasis or say "a single line, not one per export". Not blocking.
- **(d) "a package that moved or was renamed is not deleted".** The proof sentence is "no workspace manifest carries its name", and that is what the gate reads (WP-R5). It excludes a same-name move (a directory rename). A package renamed to a new *name* in a new directory has no manifest carrying the old name and passes as deleted — correctly, since the old published name is gone for every consumer and the FROM line's TO side names the successor; but the parenthetical over-reads the proof. Should-fix: "moved (its directory renamed)". Not blocking.
- **(e) The `fixed` group read literally (PR body).** Accepted: see ①-2. `linked` and `ignore` are not named by the ruling and are rightly not read.
- **(f) No ablation (PR body).** Accepted for a `scripts/**` change under os-dev's rule; each WP red asserts its refusal text, and the first-consumer pair (#26365 head `bde1e722` exit 1 with each refusal naming `@object-ui/plugin-ai#*`; probe `f4d766b5` exit 0) is the end-to-end witness. That pair is the dev's measurement, not re-run here (read-only); it is consistent with the code path and with `main` (plugin-ai: non-private, `types: dist/index.d.ts`, `src/index.tsx` present, listed in `fixed`, imported by no metadata surface).
- **(g) `open_questions`: none in report 6445436951.** The two earlier open questions on the card (D8 predicate 4; whole-package removal A vs B) are closed by decision A (6433464805) and ruling A (6439038287). Nothing left to escalate from the reports.
- **(h) Out-of-scope finding (report): #26365 needs two changeset edits.** Correctly left to that PR; the ruling itself assigns them there.
- **(i) Draft and approval state — escalated to the seat, not a diff matter.** The PR body says "The PR is draft" and the claim says "Tier H: draft only", but `pr.json` reads `draft: false`, and one `APPROVED` review (os-zhuang, 2026-10-27T15:09:21Z, at this head) is on file — the relay's `pr_create` reviewer request (#26617) produced an approval before this record existed. The seat's comment 6445680015 says auto-merge is off and the approval "stays on file and is not dismissed"; with this record FAIL the seat must not re-arm auto-merge, and the approval does not survive the must-fix push in any case (a new head).
- **(j) Reviewer-request deviation (report deviation 2).** Noted; nobody was asked to approve by the dev. Consistent with (i).

**Must-fix, before a PASS on a new head:**
1. Predicate 2 for `PACKAGE#*`: restore D9's reading. Text: "no metadata surface outside it names it in code (comment spans masked): an import specifier, by its root or a subpath, or any other occurrence of the package name". Gate: refuse on the first comment-masked occurrence outside the package's own files (the import-specifier reader becomes the special case that reports the specifier line), plus one WP red where a `*.zod.ts` or object definition carries the package name in a string value, G3 (comment only) staying green. Then re-pin the WP floor.
2. The closed vocabulary: add a third `runtime-export-retired` marker line with the `PACKAGE#*` operand (spelled exactly as the existing two lines spell their placeholders) to the 2026-08-13 addendum's code block and to the 2026-10-12 addendum's code block, and change "two operand kinds" to three, each with a short "(amended 2026-10-27, #26220)" tag, so the grammar the ADR declares closed is the grammar `parseExportOperand` accepts.

Should-fix in the same push: ③-c and ③-d wording.
